Summary of what we covered
- Use case: high-volume conversational assistant + nightly batch reranking for search re-ranking and embeddings refresh.
- Priority: low latency for conversational paths (p95 < 400ms) and predictable throughput for synchronous traffic.
- Concern: autoscaling behavior during marketing-driven traffic spikes and cost predictability.

Open items / requests from your side (so I captured correctly):
1) Expected steady-state QPS and peak QPS for inference (conversational path) and reranker jobs.
2) Typical token lengths for prompts & re-ranking requests.
3) Security/PKI requirements for private deployment (mTLS vs API keys).
4) Any internal constraints on queuing/latency budgets for queued requests.

Next steps (proposed)
- Technical deep-dive with Aditya & Marcus to walk through SDK setup, auth options, routing/fallback policies, and structured output/tool calling (we can include suggestions for embedding + reranker flow). 60–90 min. (Action: Olivia to confirm availability)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers and confirmations from our side before the deep-dive:

- Steady-state conversational QPS: ~120 QPS (mostly business hours). Peak QPS: up to ~600 QPS during promotions (spikes last 10–20 minutes).
- Reranker batch jobs: 10–12 batch jobs nightly, each job spikes CPU/GPU usage for ~30–45 minutes.
- Typical token lengths: conversational prompts avg 120 tokens request / 80 tokens response; reranker inputs avg 300 tokens.
- Security: we prefer mTLS for dedicated private deployments; API keys acceptable for hosted dev environments.
- Queuing: for conversational queries, acceptable end-to-end latency SLA is 500ms; we can accept queued processing only for reranker/batch jobs.

Hi Olivia / Samir —

Thanks — great numbers and really helpful. A few technical notes to set expectations for the deep-dive; I’ll plan to demo these items and share a sample config.

Auth & SDK setup
- We support API key auth for hosted and mTLS for private deployments; for your dedicated private deployment we can provision client certs and integrate with your PKI.
- SDKs: we have JS + Python SDKs with built-in retry/backoff, streaming, and built-in structured output helpers (schema validation).

Routing & model variants
- Smart routing rules: you can route by latency vs cost (conversational -> low-latency model variant pinned to dedicated pool; reranker -> high-throughput quantized variant).
- Automatic fallback: when dedicated capacity is saturated we can failover to a fallback pool (hosted or burst capacity) per route policy.

Structured output / tool calling
- We support function/tool calling patterns (JSON schema) with helper libraries that validate tool response shapes and surface partial results during streaming.
- For conversational flows that call external tools, we recommend isolating tool calls to a separate short-lived RPC to limit token blowup in main generation path.

Embeddings & reranker flow
- Suggested pattern: compute embeddings on write, store vectors in your vector DB; use a small dense retriever -> re-rank with a dedicated reranker model hosted on the dedicated pool.
- We recommend batching embeddings / reranker requests (we have batching helpers that amortize kernel setup and reduce per-vector cost).

Autoscaling, throughput sizing & queues (initial guidance based on your numbers)
- Baseline: on A100-class cards we typically see ~70–120 conversational sequences/s per GPU depending on model/token lengths. For your steady-state 120 QPS, 2–3 GPUs should cover steady traffic (account for KV cache and batching).
- Peak sizing: for 600 QPS short spikes, we suggest a mix of reserved baseline capacity (3 GPUs) + burst capacity via autoscaling up to 8 GPUs. Use a short-term warm pool (pre-warmed workers) to reduce cold-start latency.
- Concurrency limits: cap concurrent requests per GPU to avoid OOMs; for your token lengths we recommend max 40 concurrent conversational sessions per GPU.
- Queue strategy: keep conversational path routed to dedicated low-latency pool (no long queues) and set a short queue timeout (200–300ms). For reranker/batch jobs, route to a separate queue with configurable concurrency and longer timeouts; use job backpressure and batching window (100–200ms) to increase throughput.

Attachments: I’ve attached a sample autoscaling config and a short rule-of-thumb sheet for GPU sizing. We’ll walk through these in the call.

Looking forward to Tue 1/12 11:00 PST. I’ll prep a short demo showing routing & autoscaling behavior under synthetic loads.
